one_line: Cairnly sells supply forecasting and multi-distributor ordering software to independent US dental practices, priced per location per month.
headline: Cairnly targets a real cross-distributor ordering gap at independent dental practices, but traction is five paying customers and savings data is internal, n=5.

status_quo.body: In independent practices, the office manager orders supplies alongside front desk work. She walks the supply closet, updates a spreadsheet, and largely accepts the distributor rep's suggested reorder monthly. Gaps are filled from Amazon Business or a second distributor at retail prices, and invoices are matched by hand at month end. The deck puts this at about 5 hours a week, on spend of 6-8% of revenue. 17 of 22 interviewed practices use two or more distributors.

failure_modes.body: The core failure is who writes the order. The distributor's rep suggests the reorder, and the office manager lacks time and data to challenge it. None of 22 interviewed practices forecast usage from the schedule, so stockouts appear only when the closet is empty: 3 critical-item stockouts per quarter; one owner rescheduled patients. No tool sees total spend across sources, and her absence halts ordering. The owner bears the cost but not the work, which likely explains why the rep's default persists.

alternatives.name: Spreadsheet and supply-closet walk
alternatives.how_used: Office manager counts the closet and updates a spreadsheet alongside front desk duties.
alternatives.where_it_breaks: Depends on one person and one computer; no usage forecast, so critical items run out.

alternatives.name: Distributor rep and ordering portal
alternatives.how_used: Rep visits monthly and suggests the reorder; portal is free with the distributor account.
alternatives.where_it_breaks: Locked to one catalog; the seller writes the order and nobody has time to check it.

alternatives.name: Group purchasing organizations
alternatives.how_used: Negotiate member discounts with suppliers on behalf of practices.
alternatives.where_it_breaks: Addresses price only; the office manager still counts, orders and reconciles by hand.

alternatives.name: Horizontal inventory apps
alternatives.how_used: Generic stock tracking for practices wanting something beyond a spreadsheet.
alternatives.where_it_breaks: No link to the procedure schedule, so they track stock without forecasting use.

market_structure.body: Two national distributors control most supply distribution, each with its own ordering portal, so the free tool every practice has is built to keep orders in one catalog. Group purchasing organizations negotiate price without touching ordering. DSOs are consolidating practices and centralizing purchasing, squeezing independents on price. That gives independents a reason to buy Cairnly, though consolidation may shrink their pool (inference). Cairnly estimates about 135,000 US practices, roughly 70% independent; this company estimate is unverified.

wedge.body: Cairnly targets multi-distributor independents lacking purchasing teams. It forecasts usage from practice-management schedules and orders across distributors at contracted prices, unlike single-catalog portals, price-only GPOs or schedule-blind apps. The CEO ran operations for 8 years at a 30-location dental group. Evidence is thin: 14 pilots, 5 paying $249 per location monthly, and 11% savings over 90 days (internal data, five practices). Unverified: distributors continuing to permit third-party ordering, integration coverage, and savings beyond one quarter. Slide 8 was unreadable.

thesis_support_rationale: Sources document the workflow and its failures well through 22 interviews, but proof that Cairnly wins and holds customers rests on 5 paying practices and an internal n=5 savings figure, with distributor access untested.
evidence_gaps: No evidence distributors permit third-party ordering or share contracted prices with Cairnly.
Savings figure is internal, 90 days, five practices; no baseline method or retention data.
No practice management system integration coverage shown; supported systems are unstated.
Slide 8 unreadable; no win/loss data against distributor portals or GPOs.
diligence_questions: How do distributors respond when Cairnly places orders, and is contracted pricing access secured in writing?
Of 14 pilots, why have only 5 converted to paid, and what did the other 9 say?
Which practice management systems do you integrate with, and what share of independents do they cover?

claims.statement: Office managers spend about 5 hours a week on ordering and invoice reconciliation.
claims.quote: Office managers spend about 5 hours a week on ordering and reconciling invoices.

claims.statement: Interviewed practices reported 3 critical-item stockouts per quarter.
claims.quote: Practices we interviewed reported 3 stockouts of a critical item per quarter.

claims.statement: The rep's suggested order is the default because nobody checks it.
claims.quote: Most said the rep's suggested order is the default because nobody has time to check it.

claims.statement: Office managers accept rep orders without comparing prices.
claims.quote: I order whatever the rep puts in front of me. I don't have time to compare prices.

claims.statement: Most interviewed practices buy from multiple distributors.
claims.quote: 17 of 22 practices buy from two or more distributors

claims.statement: The spreadsheet process depends on a single person.
claims.quote: Our spreadsheet lives on one computer. When I was on vacation nobody ordered anything.

claims.statement: Distribution is concentrated in two national distributors with their own portals.
claims.quote: Supply distribution is concentrated in two national distributors who run their own ordering portals.

claims.statement: DSO consolidation squeezes independent practices on price.
claims.quote: DSOs are consolidating practices and centralizing purchasing, which squeezes independents on price.

claims.statement: Cairnly has 5 paying customers at $249 per location per month.
claims.quote: 5 paying customers at $249 per location per month

claims.statement: The 11% savings figure comes from internal data on five practices.
claims.quote: Pilot practices cut supply spend 11% on average over 90 days (internal data, n=5)

claims.statement: The CEO has dental group operations experience relevant to purchasing.
claims.quote: 8 years running operations for a 30-location dental group

claims.statement: Distributors that run their own portals may resist a third party routing orders across catalogs, which would threaten the wedge.
